index 0000000..da72c28
--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelog.d/1457.change.md
@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+Passing `kw_only=True` to `attrs.define()` / `attr.s()` now only applies to the attributes that are defined in the decorated class -- inherited attributes keep whatever they were given by their own class.
+This makes the behavior consistent with `dataclasses`.

 A(a=1)
 ```
 
-`kw_only` may also be specified at decorator level, and will apply to all attributes:
+`kw_only` may also be specified at decorator level, and will apply to all attributes that are defined in that class:
 
 ```{doctest}
 >>> @define(kw_only=True)
@@ -171,6 +171,19 @@ TypeError: __init__() takes 1 positional argument but 3 were given
 A(a=1, b=2)
 ```
 
+Just like with {mod}`dataclasses`, inherited attributes are left alone -- if you want them to be keyword-only too, the base class has to say so itself:
+
+```{doctest}
+>>> @define
+... class A:
+...     a: int
+>>> @define(kw_only=True)
+... class B(A):
+...     b: int
+>>> B(1, b=2)
+B(a=1, b=2)
+```
+
 If you create an attribute with `init=False`, the `kw_only` argument is ignored.
 
 Keyword-only attributes allow subclasses to add attributes without default values, even if the base class defines attributes with default values:
